question: Tell me about yourself and which experience has prepared you for investment banking at Goldman Sachs.
cvText:
Jamie Patel
University of Bristol — BSc Economics, second year, predicted 2:1.
UK retail analysis — Economics group project.
Compared three UK retailers’ public annual reports. Personally built the Excel revenue comparison and checked each figure against its source. Found that the fastest headline growth was driven by new stores, so growth alone did not establish stronger performance in existing shops. Explained that limitation in the group presentation.
Campus Café — Part-time Team Member.
Works weekend shifts alongside university. Prioritises orders and communicates delays to customers during busy periods.
Interest: financial analysis, business performance and investment banking advisory work.
script:
I’m a second-year Economics student at Bristol, working towards a 2:1. The experience that has prepared me most for banking is a retail analysis project, where I compared three companies’ annual reports. My part was building the revenue comparison in Excel and checking the figures back to their sources.

One company had the fastest growth, but when I looked more closely, new stores were driving it. That meant we couldn’t simply say its existing shops were performing better. I explained that distinction in our presentation. It taught me to check what sits behind a headline number before drawing a conclusion.

Alongside my degree, I work weekend café shifts. That’s helped me stay organised and communicate clearly when several customers need something at once.

Those experiences are why I want to develop in investment banking at Goldman Sachs: I’m interested in its advisory work on acquisitions and financing, where understanding a business and explaining the evidence matter. I’d bring that care with the detail, while learning how advisers turn analysis into a recommendation.
tip: Start with your studies, then choose one experience. Explain what you personally did, what you found and what it taught you. Finish by connecting that to banking. A specific conclusion beats a list of tasks. You don’t need to recite every line of your CV.
